title: The Hungry Bell
premise: When Lior Okonkwo returns to the family house to bury their twin brother Theo, they discover the body was not Theo's — and the surviving twin may be the one in the grave. The house's mirrors begin reflecting each room one second behind reality, and in that lagged second Lior glimpses the thing wearing their brother's face, a hungering presence the family's ancestors bound to the estate and paid off with one member per generation. As the lag widens and the count of doors in the house keeps changing, Lior realizes the inheritance was never money but a debt, and their lifelong invisibility — the family's habit of never photographing, never naming, never claiming the youngest — was a shield. To end it, Lior must claim the name and the debt at once, walking into the mirrored second where the bell that summons the thing still hangs, and ring it themselves, trading the family's survival for their own reflection.
about_author: Mara Amberdale is the pen name of a former estate archivist who spent six years cataloguing the belongings of houses nobody wanted to inherit. They write horror about families who keep ledgers instead of love, and they still count the doors in every room they enter.

chapters.title: The Wrong Sibling
chapters.summary: Lior returns to the Okonkwo house for Theo's funeral, numb and estranged. At the viewing, they notice the body's hands lack Theo's scar. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: grief curdling into dread as the first certainty cracks.

chapters.title: House of Counted Doors
chapters.summary: Lior stays to help their mother, Ada, settle the estate and notices the ritual: doors counted aloud each night, mirrors draped in the hall. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: the uncanny comfort of a family ruled by rules nobody explains.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: Lior's own reflection lags — a heartbeat behind every movement, smiling a fraction too long. They tell themselves it's grief. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: rationalization straining against the first undeniable wrongness.

chapters.title: What Theo Kept
chapters.summary: Searching Theo's room, Lior finds a ledger of family names, dates, and payments — one name crossed out per generation, Theo's entry freshly inked. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: the cold discovery that grief was scheduled.

chapters.title: Mother Knows the Count
chapters.summary: Ada catches Lior with the ledger and admits the family pays a debt, but insists Theo is dead and the account settled. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: a mother's love expressed as denial and arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Bell in the Well
chapters.summary: Aunt Nkechi arrives uninvited, sober for once, and tells Lior of the well behind the orchard where a bell hangs below the water — the thing that calls the debt-collector home. POV: Nkechi. Emotional beat: drunken prophecy, half confession, half warning.

chapters.title: Lag Widening
chapters.summary: The mirrors fall two seconds behind; in the delay Lior sees Theo's reflection standing where they stand, mouthing help me. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: hope and horror fused — the brother may be alive inside the lag.

chapters.title: The Photograph That Isn't
chapters.summary: Lior finds no photos of themselves anywhere in the house, no school records, no birth certificate — Ada admits the youngest is left unclaimed so the ledger can't find them. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: protection revealed as erasure, love revealed as disappearance.

chapters.title: Cousin at the Window
chapters.summary: A cousin no one remembers inviting appears at dinner, charming and slightly delayed, like a reflection. Lior counts the doors: there is one too many. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: the intruder inside the family's own rituals.

chapters.title: The Debt-Collector's Face
chapters.summary: Lior confronts the cousin, who wears the faces of every crossed-out name and offers Lior a deal: stay unclaimed and live unseen, or take the name and the debt. POV: the cousin. Emotional beat: temptation — invisibility has kept Lior safe and small their whole life.

chapters.title: Ada's Confession
chapters.summary: Ada breaks: the body in the casket was a stranger paid to be Theo; the real Theo answered the bell to spare the next generation, and the lag means he's still partly here. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: a mother's guilt finally spoken aloud.

chapters.title: Three Seconds
chapters.summary: The lag reaches three seconds. In the mirrored delay the house appears as it was a century ago, full of crossed-out ancestors, all turning to look at Lior. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: the past is not past; it is waiting in the delay.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Blank Page
chapters.summary: Lior studies the ledger and finds a blank page with their own name half-written, waiting for ink — and realizes claiming the name is the only way to close the account. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: the terrible logic that identity is both the trap and the key.

chapters.title: Nkechi's Last Sober Hour
chapters.summary: Nkechi, who once tried to ring the bell herself, gives Lior the iron key from her own failed attempt and the rule: the bell must be rung by a claimed Okonkwo, freely. POV: Nkechi. Emotional beat: a coward's redemption, passed on like an heirloom.

chapters.title: Doors Out of Count
chapters.summary: The house turns on the family: doors multiply and miscount, rooms repeat, the debt-collector walks the halls wearing Theo's face, herding them toward the mirrors. POV: Theo, inside the lag. Emotional beat: a trapped brother fighting to warn the family he was taken from.

chapters.title: Getting Them Out
chapters.summary: Lior leads Ada and the household out by counting doors against the ledger's floor plan, refusing to look at any mirror, as the collector offers them each their heart's reflection. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: courage as stubborn arithmetic — counting when counting could kill you.

chapters.title: The Name Claimed
chapters.summary: At the property line Ada finally speaks Lior's name aloud, claiming them fully — and the lag snaps shut around Lior like a door, marking them as the account's final holder. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: love as sacrifice; the shield was also the cage.

chapters.title: Down to the Water
chapters.summary: Lior walks back through the orchard at night, the house's every window reflecting them one second late, and descends to the well where the bell hangs black beneath still water. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: terrible calm — the invisible one, finally seen by everything.

chapters.title: Ring the Bell
chapters.summary: In the mirrored second, Theo's remnant holds the collector's face still while Lior takes the rope; the collector offers Theo's life back if Lior walks away unclaimed. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: the choice between the brother and the self.

chapters.title: The Count Reaches Zero
chapters.summary: Lior rings the bell, naming themselves with each strike; the debt-collector collapses into every crossed-out ancestor, who one by one turn and walk into the mirrors, closing the account. Theo's remnant fades, thanking them. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: release — grief finally allowed to be grief.

chapters.title: Reflections on Time
chapters.summary: The house stands ordinary: mirrors punctual, doors countable, the well dry. Lior, now documented and named, buries the stranger from the casket properly and hangs the ledger's last page blank forever. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: quiet aftermath — identity chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: The Hungry Bell
chapters.summary: Months later, in a city apartment, Lior's new mirror lags — half a second, once. They smile, count their doors, and begin to write. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: horror as inheritance — some bells are never fully silenced, and Lior intends to be ready.
